requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen: Today and All smart rows, then six lists with coloured icons and open counts. Counts update after completing, deleting or adding a task.

Open tasks come first, then a blue 'Completed (9)' header that collapses and expands with a chevron. Tapping the checkbox completes a task (orange check) and it moves to Completed after a short delay. Reopening also works.

The New Task sheet has title, notes, a Due Date switch with an inline calendar, a Priority menu (None/Low/High) and a List picker. Add stays disabled until there is a title. Tapping a row opens a Details sheet that saves edits.
Overdue dates are red with an exclamation icon and the word 'Overdue'. High priority shows red '!!!' and low priority a grey '!'. Today and All show the list name with a coloured dot.
Swipe-to-delete is the system trailing action. Reordering works with system reorder handles under '…' > Edit Tasks, and the new order persists. Dragging a row outside Edit mode did not reorder it.

Create works from an alert with a text field. Rename and Delete are in the list's '…' menu, and delete asks for confirmation. The main screen's Edit mode also offers delete, info and reorder for lists.
Completions, deletions, reorders and new or deleted lists all survived relaunch.

tells: The blue add button floats in the bottom-right corner, more like an Android floating action button than a toolbar item, and it covers the trailing swipe-delete button on the last row.
In the main screen's Edit mode, a stray vertical hairline separates the reorder-handle column.
In the inline calendar the selected day is a black circle instead of the tint colour.
On the task screens the large title gives way to a small centred inline title once scrolled; in Edit mode on the main screen the title is inline only.
A.scroll: The 134-row All list drags and flings like a native table, with no blank rows or pop-in, and it rubber-bands at the top. The insets and the scroll-edge blur under the bar look right.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen: Today and All, then lists in alphabetical order with open counts, plus a footer hint 'Touch and hold a list to rename it.' The lists have no icons or colours.
Open tasks come first, then a 'Completed (N)' row with a chevron. It starts collapsed and expands to show blue checked rows. Checkboxes toggle and counts update.

The New Task sheet has title, notes, a Due Date switch with a compact date picker, Priority (None/Low/Medium/High) and List. Save is hidden, not disabled, until there is a title. Tapping a row opens Edit Task, and edits save.
Overdue dates are red with the word 'Overdue'. High priority shows red '!!!' and low a grey '!'. Today and All show the list name.
Every row has a grip, and dragging it reorders immediately. Swipe left reveals a red Delete pill, which works.

Create works, rename works from the pencil button, and delete is in a touch-and-hold context menu with confirmation. A newly created list cannot be tapped or opened until the app is relaunched, and it is missing from the accessibility tree. Delete is hard to discover: the only hint mentions rename.
New tasks, edits, reorders, deletes and lists all survived relaunch.

bugs: A newly created list shows on the Lists screen but does nothing when tapped, and VoiceOver cannot see it, until the app is relaunched. Reproduced twice.
tells: Task lists are plain, edge-to-edge rows with a hairline above the first row, and separators are missing under some rows, for example after 'Read Priya' and 'Water train tickets'.
With the large title collapsed, the inline nav title sits over sharp, un-blurred row text, so the two overlap and are hard to read.
Save and Done buttons vanish when they can't be used instead of showing as disabled.
The Due Date switch has no accessibility label.
The only way to delete a list is a touch-and-hold menu; there is no Edit mode or swipe on the Lists screen.
At the largest text size, user-list rows wrap their chevron onto a line of its own while the Today and All rows don't; the checkboxes and grips don't scale with the text.
Rows look sparse: no list icons or colours, and dates include the year ('Nov 16, 2026'), which is unlike Reminders.
B.scroll: Dragging and flinging the All list is smooth, with no blank rows or pop-in, and it bounces at the top. Under the inline title the rows show through sharply instead of blurring.

why: Both apps cover the whole spec. In B, though, a newly created list can't be opened until the app restarts, and its list deletion is hidden behind an undiscoverable long press. A feels like Reminders, with list icons and colours, an inline calendar, system Edit mode and swipe actions, and correct separators. B's plain list has missing separators and a title that overlaps sharp row text.
